game: NE @ MIA Week 8 2026, morning of kickoff. Spread MIA +7 / NE -7, total 41, implied NE 24.0 / MIA 17.0. Kickoff time, open-to-current move, and weather not saved. Venue outdoor (Hard Rock) assumed only as a label; no forecast in the pack.

script.base: Books have NE leading a modest 24-17 type game, not a shootout (total 41). Miami's offense is the Ollie Gordon run game (52 carries, 291 yards over weeks 4/5/7) plus Malik Willis scrambles (16/124), so they grind early. NE's recent mix is a committee (Stevenson 33/122, Kiner 21/122, Henderson 14/62, Maye 11/80) and a short-middle pass game (Henry 16 targets, 163 yards on 68 air). Base flow: NE up by about a score late, pace moderate, both clubs run-leaning, Henry stays a 5-target intermediate piece through three quarters, Gordon keeps the Miami backfield, Jaylen Wright stays a change-of-pace.
script.flip1: NE is up 14+ early, clocks it with Stevenson/Kiner, and Maye/Henry volume stalls after halftime the way a favorite's pass game dies in a 38-21 script. Miami then abandons Gordon, so Wright can pick up garbage carries and Washington/Willis pass volume rises in a lost cause.
script.flip2: It stays inside one score or tracks toward the high 20s each, above a 41 total. Both passing games stay live (Douglas air yards 171, Washington air yards 163), and the run-lean (Maye, Gordon, Wright under) is the side that misses if Miami throws 35+ and NE never sits on the ball.

Douglas (17/174/171 air) and Brown (16/75/248 air) are the air-yard duo into the less-generous outside zones. On Miami, Dulcich (10 targets, 123 yards, 73 air) is the cleaner fit into NE's 11.74 middle, but 28.5 has no two-sided price. Washington (16/137/163 air) is the volume WR but the air-yard profile can land on NE's 5.71 right side, so that overlap is not clean.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Henry: Miami finally bracketed the middle, Douglas (171 air yards) and Brown (248 air) took the shots into the 7.2-7.6 outside zones, and a 14-point NE lead by the second quarter cut Henry to the 44-yard miss or worse. He had only 16 targets across three games, so one quiet week at 45.5 is always live, and there is no coverage chart to prove he actually sees those middle defenders. Wright: NE's 16 explosives of 10+ in seven games showed up on his first carry, a 20-yard gain, and a second-half blowout handed him the garbage series Gordon usually keeps. 14.5 is one play, his snap share is not in the pack, and laying -117 on a backup under is how a stale line still beats you. That counter is real but not stronger than 11/7/11/8 behind a healthy 52-carry Gordon, which is why the leg stays a lean instead of a pass.
slip_story: One 24-17 role-stability card, not a shootout stack and not a mix of an under with same-game overs that need 50 points. NE's intermediate TE gets the Miami middle in a 24-point team total; Miami's backup does not become a 15-yard rusher while Gordon is the offense. Shared kill is flip 1 (blowout): Henry's second-half routes die and Wright's garbage carries appear together. No TD legs, one market per player, two legs only.
